notes: Searches used: 16 (cap). Summaries blend pages, so some attributions are to the page whose title matched the query; marked in claim evidence. Textbook: none used. Not retrievable from allowed hosts: WHO complications list beyond dysphagia/aspiration pneumonia (snippet cut off), carotid ultrasound, DVT page-level source (Stroke Association via summary). Draft first-pass counts: 37 of 73 sentences needed edit or removal. EXISTING PAGE ENTRY (not edited): (1) definition says ischaemic is 85%: NHLBI result said roughly 87% (a Nigerian study ~88%); 85% not supported by anything retrieved. (2) overview 'Brain tissue dies within minutes' and 'works only in the first hours' not retrieved; NHS says clot-dissolving treatment is most effective as soon as possible. (3) diagnosis: 'Immediate CT', 'CT or MR angiography', blood glucose 'to exclude hypoglycaemia', 'echocardiography' and 'carotid ultrasound' not retrieved from NHS pages (NHS lists blood tests, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG); also a number-free but unsourced phrase. (4) treatment: 4.5 hours for thrombolysis and ~6 hours for thrombectomy are supported by NHS/NICE summaries, up to 24 hours in selected people supported by NICE summary; but the numbers sit in prose, which the authoring rules disallow. 'Then antiplatelet drugs, statins, blood pressure control' is broadly consistent (NICE advised against starting statins immediately in acute stroke but continuing existing ones); 'anticoagulation if AF is found' and the bleed treatments (reversal of anticoagulants, blood pressure control, surgery) not retrieved. (5) causes/riskFactors: arterial dissection in younger people, vascular malformations, 'excess alcohol' and 'age' not retrieved (NHS lists high BP, diabetes, AF, high cholesterol, and prevention via not smoking, diet, exercise, less alcohol). (6) complications: 'Seizures' not retrieved (WHO snippet began a long-term list with post-stroke epilepsy, so plausible); 'Permanent disability' consistent with CDC. (7) seekCare: 'Call emergency services immediately' consistent; 999 named later in the text; CDC FAST wording is US. (8) The 'TIA' alias is listed as a stroke alias and urlAlias; NHS and Stroke Association treat a TIA as a separate condition that is a warning sign, so the alias may mislead.
